name: Ghost Frequency — Pirate Music Underground
description: Ghost Frequency is an underground music scene organized around live performance in unlicensed spaces — ghost markets, abandoned infrastructure, Shelf rooftops — broadcasting simultaneously on pirated BCI channels that let audience members feel music as direct neural sensation rather than just hear it. Performers called Ghosts compose specifically for BCI delivery, layering emotional data and synthetic memory fragments into their sets alongside conventional sound. The scene's defining ethic is ephemerality: no recordings, no archives, no replays — each performance exists only in the memories of those present, which members call 'the only honest distribution model.' Corporate music corponations have attempted multiple stings to seize Ghost equipment and prosecute for unlicensed BCI broadcasting.
cultural_impact: Ghost Frequency has fundamentally changed how a generation of Shelf and Tier 2 youth think about music ownership and experience, while the BCI-delivered emotional layer has created genuine dependency in some regular attendees who describe withdrawal symptoms when unable to attend performances.
key_figures: Scene archivist 'The Contradiction' (keeps records in secret, violating scene ethics)
locations: The Antenna, abandoned broadcast tower Block 3
story_hooks: Meridian Wound's last performance contained a BCI data packet that wasn't music — it was an encrypted corporate document that audience members are now unknowingly carrying in their neural caches.

The Contradiction's secret archive has been stolen, and whoever has it now possesses the only records of Ghost Frequency performances — including one that contains evidence of a corporate crime witnessed by the audience.

A Ghost Frequency attendee has been hospitalized with severe BCI feedback damage after a performance — and the investigation reveals the Ghosts' equipment was remotely hijacked mid-set by an unknown party.
